name: arc-zero-pocket-recolor
description: Use when an ARC grid has 5-valued walls and irregular 0 regions. Identify pocket-like zero areas and recolor the small and large cavities.
---

# ARC: recolor zero pockets between 5s

## Trigger
A grid contains a field of 0s and irregular 5-valued lines/blocks. Some zero areas look trapped in bays or pockets carved out by the 5 pattern, while other 0s form the ordinary exterior background.

## Observed transformation
In demonstrated examples, leave the 5s and ordinary background 0s unchanged. Recolor the small pocket-like zero region to 7 and the larger pocket-like zero region to 8. Pocket regions may touch the grid edge (for example, a small pocket at a corner or along the top edge), so do not classify candidates solely by whether they touch the outer border. The observed examples had a small 1–2-cell pocket colored 7 and a larger pocket (10 or 22 cells) colored 8; this is a relative-size distinction, not a proven fixed threshold.

## Procedure
1. Map the 0 regions using orthogonal (up/down/left/right) connectivity; do not treat diagonal contact as connectivity.
2. Distinguish pockets carved/delineated by the 5 walls from the broad exterior zero background. Consider the shape and surrounding 5 boundaries, including bays that open at the grid boundary. A naive flood-fill from all border zeros is insufficient because demonstrated pockets can touch a border.
3. Preserve all 5 cells and all unrelated 0 regions. Recolor the small isolated pocket to 7 and the larger pocket to 8, matching the demonstrated relative-size convention.
4. Check every output cell against the input: only selected pocket zeros should change; dimensions must stay the same.

## Evidence / caution
Two examples showed a 10-cell internal pocket colored 8 and a singleton edge pocket colored 7; another showed a 22-cell pocket colored 8 and a two-cell top-edge pocket colored 7. A subsequent test with a two-cell upper-left pocket colored 7 and a 10-cell upper-central pocket colored 8 was accepted. This is an empirical task-family pattern, not a universal rule for all ARC grids; request another demonstration if candidate pockets or their ranking is ambiguous and the demo budget allows it.",

# ARC: recolor zero pockets between 5s

## Trigger
A grid contains a field of 0s and irregular 5-valued lines/blocks. Some zero areas look trapped in bays or pockets carved out by the 5 pattern, while other 0s form ordinary exterior background.

## Observed transformation
In demonstrated examples, leave the 5s and ordinary background 0s unchanged. Recolor the small pocket-like zero region to 7 and the larger pocket-like zero region to 8. Pocket regions may touch the grid edge (including a corner or top edge), so do not classify candidates solely by whether they touch the outer border. Demonstrated small 1–2-cell pockets were colored 7; larger 10- or 22-cell pockets were colored 8. This suggests relative size but is not a proven fixed threshold.

## Procedure
1. Map 0 regions using orthogonal connectivity (up/down/left/right); diagonal contact does not connect regions.
2. Distinguish pockets carved/delineated by 5 walls from broad exterior zeros. Include bays that open onto a grid boundary. A naive flood-fill from all border zeros is insufficient because demonstrated pockets can touch an edge.
3. Preserve every 5 and all unrelated 0 regions. Recolor the small isolated pocket to 7 and larger pocket to 8, following the demonstrated relative-size convention.
4. Verify only selected pocket zeros changed and preserve original dimensions.

## Evidence and limits
Examples: a 10-cell internal pocket was 8 and a singleton edge pocket was 7; another had a 22-cell pocket colored 8 and a two-cell top-edge pocket colored 7. A test with a two-cell upper-left pocket colored 7 and a 10-cell upper-central pocket colored 8 was accepted. Treat this as an empirical task pattern, not a universal ARC rule. If candidate pockets or ranking are ambiguous, request another demonstration if available.",
